Pembroke (Ballsbridge, Donnybrook, Ranelagh, Sandymount) — Dublin, Ireland

🟡 Local press research

Relatively safer day Average night

In detail

The Pembroke Local Electoral Area, covering Ballsbridge, Donnybrook, Ranelagh, and Sandymount, is consistently described in Irish media and neighbourhood guides as one of Dublin's more affluent, low-crime districts, and a targeted search of Irish outlets (independent.ie, thejournal.ie, dublinlive.ie, rte.ie, herald.ie, irishmirror.ie, extra.ie) for the 2023-2026 period found little evidence of a recurring crime or anti-social-behaviour pattern in Ballsbridge, Donnybrook, or Sandymount specifically — searches for burglary, robbery, or assault reports tied to those neighbourhoods returned mostly generic real-estate or unrelated results, and general Dublin safety guides list these three areas among the city's safest. The one significant documented incident found was a serious and specific event in Ranelagh: on 2 September 2026, the Irish Times reported that four people were arrested and a man was hospitalised after a suspected knife attack at a shop in Ranelagh, described as a violent assault requiring Garda intervention. This appears to be an isolated, serious incident rather than part of an established pattern of violence in the area, and no comparable violent-crime reports were found for Ranelagh in the preceding years of coverage searched. No specific reports of daytime muggings, tourist-targeted theft, or chronic anti-social behaviour hotspots were found for any of the four neighbourhoods within Pembroke. Given the affluent, low-density, largely residential character of Ballsbridge, Donnybrook, and Sandymount, and the absence of any documented daytime safety concerns, daytime risk is assessed as low (green). The single serious, if isolated, violent incident in Ranelagh in September 2026 is enough to warrant a degree of caution after dark rather than a blanket 'no concern' rating, so night-time risk is assessed as yellow, reflecting an occasional but real capacity for serious incidents even in an otherwise low-crime area, rather than any entrenched pattern. Sources checked: The Irish Times (irishtimes.com); MSN/PA (msn.com); headtopics.com aggregating Irish crime reporting; uhomes.com Dublin area safety guide; GetMyHomeReport Dublin Crime Statistics by Area (getmyhomereport.ie).
